The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units $[F]$ and $[G]$ has units $[F][G]/(\text{action})$. These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ and let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold. A finite family of smooth functions $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ defined on an open neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ is a **regular primary constraint family** on

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units $[\chi_a]$, then $u^a$ has units energy divided by $[\chi_a]$, so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

Let $(P^{2n},\omega)$ be symplectic, and let $N=\{\chi_1=\cdots=\chi_r=0\}$ be a regular embedded level surface with $\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}=0$ on $N$. Then $\ker(\omega|_N)$ is exactly the rank-$r$ distribution spanned by the restricted Hamiltonian vector fields $X_{\chi_a}$. This distribution is involutive. Around every point of $N$, its leaves admit smooth Frobenius coordinates $(s^1,\ldots,s^r,y^1,\ldots,y^{2n-2r})$, and the local leaf space has a unique smooth closed nondegenerate two-form $\omega_{\mathrm{red}}$ whose pullback is $\omega|_N$. Thus regular first-class constraints yield a local symplectic quotient. No global orbit-space regularity follows from these hypotheses.

derivations.claim: The periodic quotient atlas makes $T^2$ a smooth manifold. By [F1], its cotangent form is $\omega=dx\wedge dp_x+dy\wedge dp_y$. The differential $dC=dp_x+a\,dp_y$ is nowhere zero, so $C^{-1}(0)$ is a regular embedded hypersurface. The canonical bracket is skew, hence $\{C,C\}=0$ and the single constraint is first class.
Contraction with $dx\wedge dp_x+dy\wedge dp_y$ gives $X_C=\partial_x+a\partial_y$. Integrating this constant vector field yields the stated flow and leaves momenta fixed.

Fix a starting point $(x_0,y_0)$ and any target first coordinate $u\in[0,1)$. For each $n\in\mathbb Z$, the flow parameter $s=n-x_0+u$ makes the first coordinate equal to $u$ modulo one and the second equal to $y_0+a(n-x_0+u)$ modulo one. The residues $na\bmod1$ are dense: for any integer $N\ge2$, divide $[0,1)$ into $N$ half-open intervals of length $1/N$. Two of the $N+1$ residues $0,a,\ldots,Na\bmod1$ lie in one interval, so for some nonzero integer $k$ and integer $r$ we have $0<\delta:=|ka-r|<1/N$; the strict lower bound follows from irrationality. Replacing $k$ by $-k$ if needed, $\delta$ is an integer multiple of $a$ modulo one. The residues $j\delta$ for $j=0,1,\ldots,\lfloor1/\delta\rfloor$ have gaps at most $\delta$ around the unit interval, so they form a $1/N$-net. Since $N$ is arbitrary, the multiples of $a$ are dense modulo one. Therefore the orbit is dense in the second coordinate for the chosen $u$; as $u$ was arbitrary, the flow orbit is dense in $T^2$.

The orbits through $(0,0,0,0)$ and $(0,1/2,0,0)$ are distinct: equality would require integers $n,k$ with $an+k=1/2$; if $n\ne0$ this would make $a$ rational, and if $n=0$ it would assert that an integer equals $1/2$. Both orbits are dense by step 3.1. Let $U$ be a saturated open subset of the constraint surface that meets the fixed-momentum torus. Its intersection with that torus is nonempty, open, and saturated. Its complement is closed and saturated; if nonempty, it contains a whole dense orbit and hence the whole torus. Therefore the intersection is the whole torus. Any quotient neighborhoods of the two distinct orbit classes have such preimages and therefore intersect, so the orbit space is non-Hausdorff. This does not contradict the local symplectic leaf spaces in [F3].

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $c>0$ be a fixed real constant.
All curves below take values in $M$; the physical reading of $c$, of a
worldline as the history of a clock or body, and of the parameter values as
times is not part of this definition and is adopted separately in the
postulates of the framework.

**(a) Regularity classes.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with
nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A
**chart representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ for a smooth
chart $(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]).

- For $k\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$ and an interior point $t_0\in I$, the map
  $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ at $t_0$** when there is a chart representative
  $x\circ\gamma$ defined near $t_0$ that is $C^k$ there in the componentwise
  Euclidean sense. This condition is independent of the chart: on the overlap
  of two chart representatives the transition map is smooth and the chain rule
  applies ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]],
  [[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). If $t_0\in I$ is an
  included endpoint of $I$, the coordinate representative and its derivatives through order $k$
  are continuous up to $t_0$ on the relative interval
  $I\cap(t_0-\delta,t_0+\delta)$ for some $\delta>0$, with derivatives at
  $t_0$ taken one-sided. For $k=\infty$ this holds at every finite order.
  Merely possessing a one-sided secant tangent, as defined next, does not
  by itself make a curve $C^1$ at the endpoint. The map $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ on $I$** when it is $C^k$ at
  every point of $I$.

- Let $b\in\mathbb R$ and $\varepsilon>0$. A curve
  $\gamma:(b-\varepsilon,b]\to M$ has **left tangent** $v\in T_{\gamma(b)}M$
  at $b$ when for one — equivalently every — chart $(U,x)$ around
  $\gamma(b)$, writing $v=\sum_{a=0}^{3}v^a\partial_a|_{\gamma(b)}$
  ([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), the
  difference quotients satisfy
  $\bigl(x^a(\gamma(t))-x^a(\gamma(b))\bigr)/(t-b)\to v^a$ as $t\uparrow b$ for
  $a=0,1,2,3$. A **right tangent** at the left end of a curve is defined
  analogously with $t\downarrow b$. Chart independence is the one-sided
  chain-rule computation for the smooth transition maps
  ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]).

- A curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ is **piecewise $C^1$** when there is a
  finite partition $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ such that for every $i$ the
  restriction of $\gamma$ to $[s_{i-1},s_i]$ is $C^1$ up to its included
  endpoints in the one-sided sense above: in every endpoint chart its
  component derivatives on the open piece have continuous one-sided limits,
  agreeing with its endpoint derivatives. Equivalently each piece has a
  $C^1$ extension to its closed parameter piece. In particular its right
  tangent at $s_{i-1}$ and left tangent at $s_i$ exist. Such a
  partition is called **admissible** for $\gamma$. The piece extensions give continuity at the
  corners; no agreement of the
  two one-sided tangents at a corner is required.

**(b) Velocity.** If $\gamma$ is $C^1$ at an interior point $t$, its
**velocity** $\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation
$[f]\mapsto(f\circ\gamma)'(t)$ on smooth germs at $\gamma(t)$, extending
[[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]] from smooth to $C^1$ curves.
Equal germ representatives agree along the curve near $t$, and the
one-variable product rule proves the derivation identity. In a chart around
$\gamma(t)$ the velocity has the component
expression

$$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(x^a\circ\gamma\bigr)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)},$$

the coordinate expression of the derivation
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]). At an
included endpoint of the domain, $\gamma'$ means the corresponding one-sided
tangent of clause (a).

**(c) Timelike worldlines.** For $k\in\{1,2,3,\ldots\}\cup\{\infty\}$,
a **$C^k$ future timelike worldline** is a $C^k$
curve $\gamma:I\to M$ whose velocity $\gamma'(t)$ is future timelike at every
$t\in I$, in the sense of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]
and [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))<0$
and $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),N_{\gamma(t)})<0$. A **piecewise-$C^1$ future
timelike worldline** is a piecewise-$C^1$ curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ whose
velocity at every point of each open piece and whose one-sided tangents at the
two ends of each piece are future timelike; the definition is applied to a map
on an arbitrary interval $I$ with nonempty interior by requiring it on every
compact subinterval of $I$. A future timelike velocity is in particular
nonzero, so every future timelike worldline is regular.

**(d) Proper time and length.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise-$C^1$
future timelike worldline and let $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ be an admissible
partition. On each open piece $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ the function

$$h_i(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}\bigl(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s)\bigr)}$$

is continuous and strictly positive: it is a finite sum of products of
continuous real functions in any chart around a point of the piece, as
$g_{ab}\circ\gamma$ and the components of $\gamma'$ are continuous
([[thm-componentwise-limits-and-continuity]],
[[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], [[def-continuity-real]]), and the
square root is continuous on $(0,\infty)$ ([[def-rational-power]],
[[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]). The continuous one-sided limits of the component derivatives, required
by the $C^1$ extension of each piece, and continuity of $g$ imply that
$h_i$ tends to the norm of the corresponding endpoint tangent. The future
timelike hypothesis on those tangents makes these limits strictly positive, and $h_i$ extends to a continuous function on
$[s_{i-1},s_i]$; hence it is Darboux integrable there
([[def-darboux-integral]], [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]). The
**proper-time increment** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is

$$\tau(b)-\tau(a):=\frac{1}{c}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\int_{s_{i-1}}^{s_i}h_i(s)\,ds,$$

and the **Lorentzian length** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is
$L_g(\gamma):=c\,(\tau(b)-\tau(a))$. For a base point $s_0\in I$ the
**proper-time function** $\tau:I\to\mathbb R$ of a future timelike worldline is
the function with $\tau(s_0)=0$ and $\tau(s)$ equal to the increment
from $s_0$ to $s$ when $s>s_0$, and minus the increment from $s$ to $s_0$
when $s<s_0$. That the increment is independent of the admissible
partition, so that $\tau$ is well defined, and that it is invariant under
increasing $C^1$ reparametrization with strictly positive derivative
(including one-sided endpoint derivatives), comparing the increment over the
actual image interval, are proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]; the display is the
value for any admissible partition.

**(e) Four-velocity.** Let $\gamma$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike
worldline and let $t$ be a parameter value at which $\gamma$ is differentiable
(interior point of a piece, or an included endpoint with its one-sided
tangent). The **four-velocity** of $\gamma$ at $t$ is

$$U(t):=\frac{c\,\gamma'(t)}{\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)}}\in T_{\gamma(t)}M .$$

By construction $g_{\gamma(t)}(U(t),U(t))=-c^2$, and
$\gamma'(t)=\bigl(\sqrt{-g(\gamma',\gamma')}/c\bigr)U(t)$ with a strictly
positive scalar factor. If $U$ is written as the derivative of $\gamma$ with
respect to proper time, $U=d\gamma/d\tau$, this is a statement proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]], not part of the
present definition.

**(f) Scope.** Proper time, length and four-velocity are defined only for
future timelike worldlines. A null or spacelike curve receives no proper time
and no four-velocity from this definition, and no limiting or distributional
extension of the square-root integrand to such curves is asserted. The
parametrization of a worldline is part of the data and is arbitrary in this
definition: no affine parameter, no geodesic equation, no completeness or
extendability of the domain, and no measurement or clock reading is assumed.
Null and spacelike regularity classes are not defined here beyond the general
$C^k$ and piecewise-$C^1$ notions of clause (a), which make no causal
requirement.

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Fix a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,T)$ with signature $(-+++)$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Here $T$ denotes the supplied smooth timelike field selecting the future cone, called $N$ in that geometric definition. Use the distinction among a spacetime, a worldline, a pointwise observer, an observer congruence, a tetrad and a chart given in [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. This definition does not make $g$ dynamical.

In this relativistic-particle model, $m>0$ is a fixed **primitive mass parameter** measured in kilograms, and $c>0$ is a fixed **primitive conversion parameter** measured in metres per second. They are parameters of the adopted physical formulation, not quantities derived by this definition. Coordinates $x^a$ in an SI chart have length units; a cotangent vector $p=p_a\,dx^a$ has units of momentum, $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, when all four coordinates are in metres. The canonical one-form $p_a\,dx^a$ therefore has action units $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Along a future-directed timelike curve with tangent $V=dx/d\lambda$, set $s:=\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$; then $d\tau=s\,d\lambda/c$, independently of the increasing regular parameter. The length action $-mc\int s\,d\lambda$ has action units. For a future unit observer $n$ and future causal covector $p$, define the model normal-observer energy and spatial momentum covector by

$$E_n(p):=-c\,p(n),\qquad q_n(p):=p+p(n)n^\flat,$$

where $n^\flat=g(n,\cdot)$. The restriction of $g^{-1}$ to covectors annihilating $n$ is positive definite, so it supplies the norm of $q_n(p)$. These are quantity definitions and unit conventions; they do not identify canonical momentum with mechanical momentum, assert that an apparatus measured these values, or establish a dynamical law.

Let $(M,g,T)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, $m,c>0$, and $L(x,V)=-mc\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$ on the future timelike tangent cone. Its fibre derivative is

$$p_a=mc\frac{g_{ab}V^b}{s},\qquad s=\sqrt{-g(V,V)}>0.$$

The velocity Hessian is $mc(g_{ab}/s+V_aV_b/s^3)$, has kernel exactly $\mathbb RV$, and rank three. The image consists exactly of the future shell $\Sigma_m^+=\{(x,p)\in T^*M:g_x^{-1}(p,p)=-m^2c^2,\ p^\sharp\text{ future}\}$. Each fibre is a connected positive ray, and the Legendre map is a surjective submersion onto this embedded image. Its energy $p(V)-L$ is zero; the map has no local inverse in the four-velocity direction.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the relativistic particle model, on top of the
flat spacetime model of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and the SI unit
conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], together with
the framework's idealisations of point particles, ideal clocks and ideal light
signals:

**(i) Mass and momentum.** Every massive classical particle of the model
carries a positive constant invariant mass parameter $m>0$ and has
four-momentum $P=mU$, where $U$ is the four-velocity of its future timelike
worldline ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]],
[[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]],
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]); $P$ is a vector of $V$
whose SI unit is kilogram metre per second. The formula is adopted only for
$m>0$; the case $m=0$ is not defined by it and is the separate premise
[[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]]. In particular $\eta(P,P)=-m^2c^2$
is a consequence of the four-velocity normalisation, not a separate
assumption.

**(ii) Observer measurement identification.** Relative to a future unit
observer $n$, the model identifies the measured energy of the particle with
$E_n(P)$, its measured spatial momentum with $q_n(P)$, its kinetic energy with
$T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ and its rest energy with $mc^2$, where $E_n,q_n,T_n$ are
the quantities of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; the
units are the joule, kilogram metre per second and kilogram of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. This clause is a formulation
convention identifying mathematical quantities with the quantities the model
calls measured; it is not a measurement report and no experiment is claimed.

**(iii) Isolated collision balance.** An isolated collision is represented by
a mass-specified on-shell collision datum at an event, with finite nonempty
incoming and outgoing lists of the massive particles of (i) and/or the ideal
massless particles of [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]], and with
no external four-momentum transfer or omitted leg. The interaction is
idealized as confined to that event. The sum of the incoming four-momenta equals the sum of the
outgoing four-momenta, in the sense of the collision data of
[[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]]: the model adopts
$Q_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\mathrm{out}}$ for such an isolated datum. No particular
collision is asserted to occur, and no mechanism, probability, cross section
or amplitude is supplied by this clause.

**(iv) Equation of motion for a stipulated force.** Put
$H_c^+:=\{U\in C^+:\eta(U,U)=-c^2\}$. A stipulated force law is a given
map $F:D\to V$ on a given subset $D\subseteq A\times H_c^+$,
with force components in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m/\mathrm s^2$. No regularity
away from the specified worldline is assumed. Along a given $C^2$ massive worldline
$x:I\to A$ with $(x(s),U(s))\in D$ for all $s\in I$, the model's particle
equation is $m\,dU/d\tau=F(x,U)$, with
$dU/d\tau$ the proper-time derivative of
[[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]], so that the stipulated $F$
is the four-force of the motion. A particular force law, and the existence,
uniqueness and domain of solutions of the resulting equation, are not adopted
here and belong to a separate model.

Empirical support for these assumptions is a nonlogical relation of the
framework, not a proof; the idealisations of point particles, ideal clocks,
ideal light signals and flat spacetime are inherited and travel to every
consumer of this premise.

Adopt [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] and
[[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]]. Then the following conditional
physical claims hold in the flat classical model, with the units of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]].

**(a) Massive particle.** Let a massive particle have constant mass $m>0$,
four-momentum $P=mU$ and a future unit observer $n$. Its measured energy
$E_n(P)=-c\,\eta(P,n)$, spatial momentum $q_n(P)=h(P)$ and kinetic energy
$T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ satisfy $E_n(P)>0$, $T_n(P)\ge0$ and the mass-shell
identity $E_n(P)^2=m^2c^4+c^2|q_n(P)|^2$; $T_n(P)=0$ if and only if the
particle is at rest in the observer's frame ($U=cn$). In an inertial frame
whose stationary observer is $n=e_0$, the components are $P=(E/c,\mathbf p)$
with $E=E_{e_0}(P)=m\gamma_wc^2$ and $\mathbf p=m\gamma_w\mathbf w\in\mathbb R^3$
the coordinates of $q_{e_0}(P)=\sum_{i=1}^3p^ie_i$
for the coordinate velocity $\mathbf w$, and under a passive boost the
components transform as the components of the vector $P$; the combination
$E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2=m^2c^4$ is frame-independent.

**(b) Four-force.** Along a $C^2$ worldline with four-acceleration $A$, the
four-force $F=\dot P$ satisfies $\eta(P,F)=0$ and $F=mA$; in an inertial frame
$F=\gamma\,(\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w/c,\ \mathbf f)$ and
$dE/dt=\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w$, where $\mathbf f=d\mathbf p/dt$ is the
coordinate three-force. The constancy of $m$ is used; if instead $m$ is a
$C^1$ function $m:I\to(0,\infty)$ along the same worldline, define $P:=mU$
and $F:=\dot P$ by the general derivative construction. As a mathematical identity, $\eta(P,F)=-mc^2\,dm/d\tau$, and the
constant-mass identities are not transferred to variable-mass systems.

**(c) System mass.** For a finite nonempty system of particles all of whose
four-momenta are nonzero future causal, let $Q:=\sum_iP_i$. If $Q$ is
future timelike, its invariant mass $M=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$ satisfies: in the
center-of-momentum frame with $e_0=Q/(Mc)$ one has
$Mc^2=\sum_iE_{e_0}(P_i)$; every massive constituent has
$E_{e_0}(P_i)\ge m_ic^2$, with equality exactly when it is at rest in that
frame, and every massless constituent has $E_{e_0}(P_i)>0$. Hence

are massless with parallel momenta, and no center-of-momentum frame exists.

$E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|>0$, has no rest frame and is not $mU$ for any $m>0$; it is

four-momentum $Q$. Then the necessary inequalities $M\ge\sum_im_i$ and

and a target of mass $m_2$ at rest in the observer frame of the target, with

cannot produce an outgoing state containing a massive particle. These are kinematic necessity statements under
the adopted conservation: they do not assert that any collision occurs, do
not fix probabilities, amplitudes or cross sections, and are not empirical
findings.

stated idealisations; the conclusions carry the same idealisations. No
measurement, precision, statistical or empirical claim is made.

Let $c > 0$ and let $(A,V,\eta,C^{+})$ be an oriented time-oriented affine
Minkowski space ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

$\eta(U(s),U(s)) = -c^{2}$ for every $s \in I$; equivalently the dimensionless

timelike. Thus the dimensionless four-velocity lies on the future unit
hyperboloid $\{v \in C^{+}:\eta(v,v)=-1\}$.

**(c) Rest space and projection.** Let $n \in V$ be future unit timelike,
$\eta(n,n) = -1$, and put $n^{\perp} := \{\,v \in V : \eta(n,v) = 0\,\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]). Then $n^{\perp}$ is a
3-dimensional linear subspace of $V$, the restriction of $\eta$ to $n^{\perp}$

linear, idempotent with $h \circ h = h$, has image $n^{\perp}$ and kernel
$\operatorname{span}(n)$, satisfies $h(n) = 0$ and $\eta(n,h(v)) = 0$ for all
$v \in V$, and every $v \in V$ has the unique decomposition
$v = -\eta(n,v)\,n + h(v)$. Moreover $|w| := \sqrt{\eta(w,w)}$ defines a norm
on $n^{\perp}$.

timelike vectors, put $\gamma := -\eta(n,u)$ and $w := c\,h(u)/\gamma$. Then
$\gamma \ge 1$, $w$ lies in $n^{\perp}$,
$u = \gamma\,(n + w/c)$, $|w|^{2} = c^{2}(1-\gamma^{-2}) < c^{2}$,
$\gamma = (1-|w|^{2}/c^{2})^{-1/2}$, and $\gamma = 1$ if and only if $u = n$.
The vector $w$ is the velocity of a worldline with four-velocity $cu$ relative
to the observer $n$, and $\gamma$ is its Lorentz factor.

**(e) Coordinate form.** Let $(o;e_0,\dots,e_3)$ be an inertial frame and let

a fixed positive constant $c$; it asserts no clock reading and identifies no

$$S_m[x]=-mc\int_I\sqrt{-g(x',x') }\,d\lambda.$$

Here λ is an increasing regular parameter, endpoint events are fixed, and admissible variations remain future timelike. The integrand is the proper-time length density, so $S_m=-mc^2\int d\tau$; its dimension is action (J s). The adopted premise concerns this ideal free test body only. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units $[F]$ and $[G]$ has units $[F][G]/(\text{action})$. These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

$C^\infty(M)$, with pointwise multiplication and the symplectic Poisson
bracket, is a real Poisson algebra.

Let $F(t,x,\lambda)$ be jointly $C^\infty$ in $(t,x,\lambda)$ on an open time-state-parameter
domain. Near any base data $(t_0,x_0,\lambda_0)$ there are a compact time
interval $I$ and a neighbourhood $W$ of $(x_0,\lambda_0)$ such that, for every
$(y,\lambda)\in W$, the solution of

$$x'(t)=F(t,x(t),\lambda),\qquad x(t_0)=y,$$

is defined on $I$, and the resulting solution map is smooth in the pair
$(y,\lambda)$.

derivations.claim: Write $X_H=A^i\partial_{q^i}+B_i\partial_{p_i}$. Contraction gives $\iota_{X_H}\omega=A^i dp_i-B_i dq^i$. Equating with $dH=H_{q^i}dq^i+H_{p_i}dp_i$ yields $A^i=H_{p_i}$, $B_i=-H_{q^i}$.

Substitution into $X_G(F)$ gives the displayed coordinate bracket. Its intrinsic definition from ω makes the formula invariant under cotangent coordinate changes; [F2] supplies the Poisson identities.
Along a solution, the chain rule gives $dF/dt=F_t+dF(X_{H_t})$; the definition of the bracket and skewness give $dF(X_{H_t})=X_{H_t}(F)=\{F,H_t\}$.

Smoothness of $H_t$ makes its coordinate Hamiltonian vector field smooth. Applying [F3] on the open domain yields unique local solutions and smooth dependence wherever solutions remain in that domain. This conclusion says nothing about extension beyond that interval.

For smooth autonomous $H$, $d\omega=0$ and $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$ imply $\mathcal L_{X_H}\omega=d\iota_{X_H}\omega+\iota_{X_H}d\omega=d^2H=0$; differentiating the pullback along the local flow therefore gives zero, and its initial value is ω, so the flow preserves ω.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ and let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold. A finite family of smooth functions $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ defined on an open neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ is a **regular primary constraint family** on

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units $[\chi_a]$, then $u^a$ has units energy divided by $[\chi_a]$, so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold as in [[def-rpm-h-cotangent-phase-space]], and write its cotangent phase space in induced coordinates $(q^i,p_i)$. With $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$, define $X_H$ by $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$ and define the Poisson bracket by $\{F,G\}:=X_G(F)$. Then

$$X_H=\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i}\frac{\partial}{\partial q^i}-\frac{\partial H}{\partial q^i}\frac{\partial}{\partial p_i},\qquad \{F,G\}=F_{q^i}G_{p_i}-F_{p_i}G_{q^i}.$$

The bracket is coordinate independent and makes smooth functions a Poisson algebra. If $H_t$ is smooth on an open time-dependent domain $D\subset\mathbb R\times T^*Q$, each solution of $\dot z=X_{H_t}(z)$ has local uniqueness and smooth dependence on initial data and parameters; on its actual interval,

$$\frac{d}{dt}F(t,z(t))=\partial_tF+\{F,H_t\}.$$

No completeness or global flow is asserted. If $H$ is smooth, each local time-$t$ flow map preserves ω.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every point $p$ of a $2n$-dimensional
symplectic manifold $(M,\omega)$, there are coordinates
$(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ centred at $p$ in which

$$\omega=\sum_{i=1}^n dq^i\wedge dp_i.$$

Let $(O,\mathcal L)$ be a time-dependent Lagrangian chart over $[a,b]\times U$ in the sense of
[[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]] and let $q:[a,b]\to U$ be a $C^2$ admissible curve.
Then $q$ is stationary for the action $S$ if and only if

$$E_{\mathcal L}(q)(t)=0\qquad\text{for every }t\in[a,b].$$

Differentiate $\chi_a(\lambda,z(\lambda))=0$ along a solution; the chain rule yields $0=\partial_\lambda\chi_a+d_z\chi_a(\dot z)$.

Substitute the vector field from step 2.1 and use [F2]: $d_z\chi_a(X_{H_c})=\{\chi_a,H_c\}$ and $d_z\chi_a(X_{\chi_b})=\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}$, giving the displayed consistency equation on $N_\lambda$. 1. $d\omega=0$, and
2. $(T_pM,\omega_p)$ is a [[def-symplectic-vector-space|symplectic vector
   space]] for every $p\in M$.

zero two-form satisfies the definition.

$$W^\omega=\{v\in V:\omega(v,w)=0\text{ for every }w\in W\}.$$

$$\dim W+\dim W^\omega=\dim V,\qquad (W^\omega)^\omega=W.$$

The $d\chi_a$ are independent, so their images under the isomorphism $\omega^\flat$ are independent; therefore these $r$ vectors are independent. The level has codimension $r$, and [F4] gives $\dim(T_zN)^\omega=r$, so they span the symplectic orthogonal.

On $N$, $d\chi_b(X_{\chi_a})=\{\chi_b,\chi_a\}=0$ by first-classness and [F7], so each $X_{\chi_a}$ is tangent. Their independence from step 1.1 implies $r\le\dim N=2n-r$, hence $r\le n$. The radical of the restricted form is $T_zN\cap(T_zN)^\omega$; since the orthogonal is already spanned by tangent $X_{\chi_a}$, this intersection is exactly that span.

For smooth kernel fields $U,V$ and any tangent field $W$, apply $d\omega_N=0$ to $(U,V,W)$. All terms containing contractions with $U$ or $V$ vanish, leaving $\omega_N([U,V],W)=0$. Thus ([U,V]) is again in the kernel and the distribution is involutive.

The Frobenius frame proof solves a transverse linear matrix ODE to straighten a local frame. Its coefficients are smooth, so [F5] gives a smooth local solution in transverse coordinates; the initial matrix is identity, so its determinant remains nonzero after shrinking the coordinate neighborhood. The resulting frame is involutive and [F6] supplies local $(s,y)$ coordinates. This explicitly supplies the parameter dependence needed in that construction.
Since every $\omega_N$-kernel vector is tangent to the $s$-leaves, the contraction of $\omega_N$ with $\partial_{s^a}$ vanishes. Therefore its coordinate expression has no $ds^a$ factor.

For each leaf vector $U$, Cartan's identity gives $\mathcal L_U\omega_N=d\iota_U\omega_N+\iota_Ud\omega_N=0$. Thus the coefficients of the remaining $dy^i\wedge dy^j$ form are independent of $s$; they define a form $\omega_{\mathrm{red}}$ on the local $y$-space and the coordinate projection pulls it back to $\omega_N$. It is closed because $d\omega_N=0$, and nondegenerate because its kernel would lift to a vector in $TN$ orthogonal to all of $TN$, hence to the already-quotiented kernel.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$** on $M$ when it is symmetric and nondegenerate, and at every
$p\in M$ the pair $(T_pM,g_p)$ is a Lorentz vector space of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]: that is, $g_p$ has
inertia $(3,1,0)$, so that some — equivalently every — basis of $T_pM$ in which
the matrix of $g_p$ is diagonal has exactly one negative and three positive
diagonal entries. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** (or
Lorentzian manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$). In a smooth chart $(U,x)$ the
**components** of $g$ are the $C^\infty$ functions
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and $g_{ab}=g_{ba}$ by symmetry.
We use indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ and the Einstein summation convention, with
components in a chart written as lower-case indexed symbols and equations
between indexed fields understood basis-independently. These conventions are
fixed once for this library and the physical reading of the symbols is recorded
with the framework postulates, separately from this mathematical definition.

**(b) Pointwise causal structure.** For every $p\in M$ the vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] applies to the Lorentz vector
space $(T_pM,g_p)$: a tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is **timelike** when
$g_p(v,v)<0$, **null** when $v\neq0$ and $g_p(v,v)=0$, **spacelike** when
$g_p(v,v)>0$, and **causal** when it is timelike or null. Every nonzero
$v\in T_pM$ has exactly one causal character. The **timelike set**
$T_p:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\}$ has exactly two connected components, each
nonempty, open, convex and path-connected; each $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $T_pM$ satisfies $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
for some ordering, so in particular nonzero orthonormal vectors exist at every
point ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]],
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

**(c) Time orientation.** A **time orientation** of $(M,g)$, also called a
**choice of future cone**, is a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]], whose tangent-bundle
smooth structure uses the axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of
[[def-countable-choice]]; this is the only use of that axiom in this
definition) such that

$$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in M .$$

The function $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N_p)$ is $C^\infty$ because $g$ is a smooth
covariant $2$-tensor field and $N$ a smooth field, so the condition is a
pointwise strict inequality between a smooth function and $0$; since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0$ implies $N_p\neq0$, a time orientation is nowhere vanishing.
A **time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** is a triple $(M,g,N)$
consisting of a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and a time orientation $N$.

Given a time orientation $N$ and $p\in M$, the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and we
**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future causal vectors form
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no
nonzero causal $v$ satisfies $g_p(v,N_p)=0$, so the definition is exhaustive and
mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and
two time orientations $N,N'$ determine the same future-directed causal vectors
at every point where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)<0$, while they determine opposite ones
where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)>0$, by
[[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]; that lemma
also shows the sign of $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ is constant on every connected
component of $M$.

**(d) The inverse metric.** Because $g_p$ is nondegenerate, it induces at each
$p$ an isomorphism $\flat_p:T_pM\to T_p^*M$, $v\mapsto g_p(v,\cdot)$, and an
inverse metric $g_p^{-1}$ on the dual space; the inverse metric, the musical
isomorphisms and the components $g^{ab}$ are defined separately on this page,
where the smoothness of those components is also proved. Neither construction
uses any choice principle beyond the one already recorded in (c).


**(e) Smooth timelike curves and their scalar normalization.** Before using
these quantities in the physical conventions, fix a positive real scaling
parameter $c$ (with no physical meaning or dimension in this mathematical
item). A **smooth future timelike curve** is a smooth map $\gamma:I\to M$
from a nonempty open real interval $I$ ([[def-interval]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) whose velocity derivation
$\gamma'(s)\in T_{\gamma(s)}M$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]]) satisfies
$g(\gamma',\gamma')<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)<0$ at every $s\in I$.
In a chart its components are $d(x^a\circ\gamma)/ds$, $a=0,1,2,3$.
For a supplied base point $s_0\in I$ and additive constant $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$
define

$$h(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s))},\qquad \tau(s):=\tau_0+\frac1c\int_{s_0}^{s}h(r)\,dr,\qquad U(s):=\frac{c\gamma'(s)}{h(s)}.$$

The integral is oriented when $s<s_0$. The function $\tau$ is called
**proper time** for this scaling and $U$ the **four-velocity** of the smooth
curve; its increment times $c$ is the Lorentzian length. The well-definedness
proof below shows $\tau'>0$, that $\tau:I\to\tau(I)$ is a smooth
diffeomorphism, and that $U$ is the velocity of $\gamma\circ\tau^{-1}$.
Thus $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and $U$ is future timelike. This introduces the smooth
case before any physical unit reading; the later worldline definition extends
it to its stated $C^k$, endpoint and piecewise-$C^1$ classes. It asserts no
clock coupling, motion law or physical value of $c$.

**Convention and scope.** The physical reading of a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold as a classical spacetime model, and the domain in which
that reading is adopted, are recorded in the framework postulate
`post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain`; the words spacetime and event carry no
mathematical content beyond this definition, and this item asserts no claim
about nature. The dimension $4$ and the absence of boundary are part of the
data; nothing in the definition assumes that $M$ is nonempty or connected, and
no completeness, extendibility or maximality property of $(M,g)$ is asserted.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold without boundary with affine connection $\nabla$, and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior. A smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ is an **affinely parametrized geodesic** when
$$D_t\gamma'(t)=0\qquad(t\in I),$$
with one-sided interpretation at an included endpoint. Constant curves are geodesics. Unless another parametrization is explicitly stated, “geodesic” means affinely parametrized geodesic.

For a given connection on $E$ and a smooth curve on an interval with nonempty interior, the **covariant derivative along the curve** is
$$D_tV=(\gamma^*\nabla)_{\partial/\partial t}V.$$
Here $V$ is a section of the pullback bundle as in [[def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve]], and the pullback connection exists by [[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. It is real-linear and satisfies $D_t(fV)=f'V+fD_tV$ for functions of the parameter.

At an included endpoint the smooth up-to-boundary coefficients have their one-sided derivative; equivalently any smooth local extension of the coefficients gives this value, because extensions agreeing on a one-sided interval have the same derivative there. For a piecewise smooth curve the derivative is defined on each piece, with separate one-sided derivatives at corners; those derivatives are not required to agree. A singleton interval carries no derivative operator under this convention and will have identity transport by definition. A zero section or a rank-zero bundle gives zero covariant derivative. Constant base curves can have sections with nonzero coefficient derivative.

Let $(O,\mathcal L)$ be a time-dependent Lagrangian chart over $[a,b]\times U$ in the sense of
[[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]] and let $q:[a,b]\to U$ be a $C^2$ admissible curve.
Then $q$ is stationary for the action $S$ if and only if

$$E_{\mathcal L}(q)(t)=0\qquad\text{for every }t\in[a,b].$$

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ and let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold. A finite family of smooth functions $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ defined on an open neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ is a **regular primary constraint family** on

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units $[\chi_a]$, then $u^a$ has units energy divided by $[\chi_a]$, so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold as in [[def-rpm-h-cotangent-phase-space]], and write its cotangent phase space in induced coordinates $(q^i,p_i)$. With $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$, define $X_H$ by $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$ and define the Poisson bracket by $\{F,G\}:=X_G(F)$. Then

$$X_H=\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i}\frac{\partial}{\partial q^i}-\frac{\partial H}{\partial q^i}\frac{\partial}{\partial p_i},\qquad \{F,G\}=F_{q^i}G_{p_i}-F_{p_i}G_{q^i}.$$

The bracket is coordinate independent and makes smooth functions a Poisson algebra. If $H_t$ is smooth on an open time-dependent domain $D\subset\mathbb R\times T^*Q$, each solution of $\dot z=X_{H_t}(z)$ has local uniqueness and smooth dependence on initial data and parameters; on its actual interval,

$$\frac{d}{dt}F(t,z(t))=\partial_tF+\{F,H_t\}.$$

No completeness or global flow is asserted. If $H$ is smooth, each local time-$t$ flow map preserves ω.

Let $(M,g,T)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, $m,c>0$, and $L(x,V)=-mc\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$ on the future timelike tangent cone. Its fibre derivative is

$$p_a=mc\frac{g_{ab}V^b}{s},\qquad s=\sqrt{-g(V,V)}>0.$$

The velocity Hessian is $mc(g_{ab}/s+V_aV_b/s^3)$, has kernel exactly $\mathbb RV$, and rank three. The image consists exactly of the future shell $\Sigma_m^+=\{(x,p)\in T^*M:g_x^{-1}(p,p)=-m^2c^2,\ p^\sharp\text{ future}\}$. Each fibre is a connected positive ray, and the Legendre map is a surjective submersion onto this embedded image. Its energy $p(V)-L$ is zero; the map has no local inverse in the four-velocity direction.

derivations.claim: Use the supplied smooth tangent and cotangent bundles under [A1], with the mathematical functionals and selected branches [F1,F2]. In a spacetime chart, variation in $e$ gives $C_m=0$. Variation in $p_a$ gives $x'^a=e g^{ab}p_b$. Variation in $x^a$, integrating the $p_a\delta x'^a$ term by parts with $\delta x$ vanishing at endpoints, gives $p'_a=-e\partial_a C_m=-\tfrac e2\partial_a g^{bc}p_bp_c$. The vertical differential of $C_m$ is $d_pC_m=p^\sharp$; it is nonzero on the massive branch because $g^{-1}(p,p)=-m^2c^2<0$, and on the massless branch because $p\ne0$ and $g^{-1}$ is nondegenerate. Thus the shell is a regular primary constraint by [F7], and [F8] fixes the canonical sign convention. The equations are tensorial and hence agree across overlapping charts.

For $m>0$, the first equation gives $p_a=g_{ab}x'^b/e$. The constraint gives $g(x',x')=-e^2m^2c^2$, so $s=\sqrt{-g(x',x')}=emc$ because $e,m,c>0$. Hence $p_a=mc\,g_{ab}x'^b/s$, the fibre derivative of the square-root Lagrangian; this agrees with the exact image result [F9].

Differentiate $p_a=g_{ab}x'^b/e$, use the second equation, and use the inverse-metric identity $\partial_a g^{bc}g_{bi}g_{cj}=-\partial_a g_{ij}$. Multiplying by $e$ gives $$g_{ab}x''^b+(\partial_cg_{ab})x'^cx'^b-\frac{e'}e g_{ab}x'^b=\frac12(\partial_ag_{ij})x'^ix'^j.$$ Since $x'^cx'^b$ is symmetric, the difference of the metric-derivative terms is $\frac12(\partial_cg_{ab}+\partial_bg_{ac}-\partial_ag_{bc})x'^cx'^b=g_{ad}\Gamma^d{}_{cb}x'^cx'^b$. Inverting $g_{ab}$ therefore gives $$\nabla_{x'}x'=\frac{e'}e x'.$$ This computation uses [F3]–[F5]; it is the coordinate form of the reparameterized geodesic equation.

Substituting $p_a=g_{ab}x'^b/e$ into the integrand gives $L_1=g(x',x')/(2e)-em^2c^2/2=-s^2/(2e)-em^2c^2/2$, where $s=\sqrt{-g(x',x')}>0$. Its $e$-derivative is $s^2/(2e^2)-m^2c^2/2$, whose unique positive zero is $e=s/(mc)$; the second derivative there is $-s^2/e^3\ne0$. Thus the $p$- and $e$-stationarity equations determine a unique smooth auxiliary pair $(p^*(x,x'),e^*(x,x'))$ on the future timelike domain, and the stationary integrand is $-mc\,s$. For any fixed-endpoint variation $x_\varepsilon$, choose $p_\varepsilon,e_\varepsilon$ by these formulas. The chain rule for the varied action has the $x_\varepsilon$ variation plus terms proportional to its $p$- and $e$-derivatives; those terms vanish at the auxiliary stationary pair. Hence the first variation of the reduced action equals the $x$-part of the first-order variation. Conversely every stationary first-order triple must equal this unique auxiliary pair, so the same identity gives the reverse implication. This proves the equivalence with the square-root action.

For $m>0$, $d\tau=s\,d\lambda/c=em\,d\lambda$, so $e=1/m$ in proper-time parameter and step 2.2 becomes $\nabla_UU=0$; the converse follows by reversing the momentum definition and the same identities.

For $m=0$, [F2] selects $p\ne0$ future null; the first equation makes $x'=e p^\sharp$, so $x'$ is nonzero future null and the constraint is null. Choose a new parameter σ with $d\sigma/d\lambda=e/e_0$ for any constant $e_0>0$; the connection transformation law applied to step 2.2 gives $\nabla_{dx/d\sigma}(dx/d\sigma)=0$. Since $g(x',x')=0$, the massive proper-time construction cannot be used.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units $[F]$ and $[G]$ has units $[F][G]/(\text{action})$. These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

An **oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space** is a quadruple
$(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ with the following data. In this notation $V$ includes its
specified orientation; forgetting that orientation gives only the underlying
real vector space, not the full datum $V$ of the model.

1. A nonempty affine space $A$ over a $4$-dimensional real vector space $V$,
   with action $(p,v)\mapsto p+v$ and displacement $q-p\in V$
   ([[def-affine-space-and-displacement]]). In particular $V$ is a real vector
   space of dimension $4$.
2. A Lorentz form $\eta$ on $V$, i.e. a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form of
   inertia $(3,1,0)$ ([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]). Its associated quadratic
   form is $q(v)=\eta(v,v)$.
3. An **orientation** of $V$: a positive ray of the determinant line
   $\Lambda^4V$, fixed once and for all
   ([[def-determinant-line-orientation-of-a-finite-dimensional-real-vector-space]]).
4. A **time orientation** $C^+$ of $(V,\eta)$: one of the two connected
   components of the timelike set $T=\{v\in V:\eta(v,v)<0\}$, the other being
   $C^-:=T\setminus C^+$ ([[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]).

The following terminology is attached to such a quadruple.

- The elements $p$ of $A$ are the **events**; for events $p,q$ the vector
  $q-p\in V$ is the **displacement from $p$ to $q$**.
- The **interval** of $p,q\in A$ is the real number
  $I(p,q):=\eta(q-p,q-p)=q(q-p)$.
- Events $p,q$ are **timelike**, **null**, **spacelike** or **causally
  related** when the displacement $q-p$ is timelike, null, spacelike or causal
  in the sense of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]; they are
  **future-related** when $q-p$ is future causal and **past-related** when
  $q-p$ is past causal in the sense of
  [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]].

**No point of $A$ is distinguished.** For every $v\in V$ the translation
$\tau_v:A\to A$, $\tau_v(p):=p+v$, is a bijection, since it is inverse to
$\tau_{-v}$: $\tau_{-v}(\tau_v(p))=(p+v)+(-v)=p+(v-v)=p$ and symmetrically, by
the affine action axioms ([[def-affine-space-and-displacement]]). Displacements
are translation invariant, $\tau_v(q)-\tau_v(p)=q-p$, so every $\tau_v$ preserves
the interval, the causal classification of every ordered pair, and the sets
$C^+$, $C^-$ (which are subsets of $V$, independent of the point of $A$); it
changes only the labelling of points. The mathematical structure of the model is
exactly the quadruple $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$; no derived physical quantity (proper
time, four-velocity, momentum, energy, charge or any field) is part of this
definition, and all later structure of the framework (frames, charts, tensor
fields, worldlines) is built on this model.

**Well-definedness.** The affine-space definition supplies the action and the
unique displacements; the Lorentz-form definition supplies $\eta$ and its
inertia; the determinant-line definition supplies orientations; and the two
components of $T$ between which the time-orientation definition chooses exist by
the components lemma recorded in the well-definedness clause of
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], which is also what makes the
names future and past causal in item 4 well defined.

Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold as in [[def-rpm-h-cotangent-phase-space]], and write its cotangent phase space in induced coordinates $(q^i,p_i)$. With $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$, define $X_H$ by $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$ and define the Poisson bracket by $\{F,G\}:=X_G(F)$. Then

$$X_H=\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i}\frac{\partial}{\partial q^i}-\frac{\partial H}{\partial q^i}\frac{\partial}{\partial p_i},\qquad \{F,G\}=F_{q^i}G_{p_i}-F_{p_i}G_{q^i}.$$

The bracket is coordinate independent and makes smooth functions a Poisson algebra. If $H_t$ is smooth on an open time-dependent domain $D\subset\mathbb R\times T^*Q$, each solution of $\dot z=X_{H_t}(z)$ has local uniqueness and smooth dependence on initial data and parameters; on its actual interval,

$$\frac{d}{dt}F(t,z(t))=\partial_tF+\{F,H_t\}.$$

No completeness or global flow is asserted. If $H$ is smooth, each local time-$t$ flow map preserves ω.

Let $(P^{2n},\omega)$ be symplectic, and let $N=\{\chi_1=\cdots=\chi_r=0\}$ be a regular embedded level surface with $\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}=0$ on $N$. Then $\ker(\omega|_N)$ is exactly the rank-$r$ distribution spanned by the restricted Hamiltonian vector fields $X_{\chi_a}$. This distribution is involutive. Around every point of $N$, its leaves admit smooth Frobenius coordinates $(s^1,\ldots,s^r,y^1,\ldots,y^{2n-2r})$, and the local leaf space has a unique smooth closed nondegenerate two-form $\omega_{\mathrm{red}}$ whose pullback is $\omega|_N$. Thus regular first-class constraints yield a local symplectic quotient. No global orbit-space regularity follows from these hypotheses.

derivations.claim: Solving the shell equation gives $p_0=-P^0$ with $P^0=\sqrt{m^2c^2+|\mathbf p|^2}>0$; for $m=0$ the exclusion $\mathbf p=0$ makes $P^0>0$. Thus $y=x^0/P^0$ and $a^i=x^i-(P^i/P^0)x^0$ are smooth shell coordinates, with inverse $x^0=yP^0, x^i=a^i+yP^i$. These formulas prove a diffeomorphism $\Sigma_m^+\cong\mathbb R_y\times B_m$.

Since the constraint depends only on $p$, [F3] gives its characteristic field $X_C=P^a\partial_{x^a}$; [F4] identifies this direction with the characteristic leaves used for reduction. The flow sends $y\mapsto y+\alpha$ while fixing $a,p$. Hence two points are in the same full orbit exactly when their $a,p$ labels agree, and the quotient map is the product projection to $B_m$.

In shell coordinates $x^0=yP^0, x^i=a^i+yP^i$, so $dx^0=P^0\,dy+y\,dP^0$ and $dx^i=da^i+P^i\,dy+y\,dP^i$. Since $p_0=-P^0$, expanding the canonical form gives $$\omega=da^i\wedge dp_i+dy\wedge(P^i dp_i-P^0dP^0)+y\,dP^i\wedge dp_i.$$ Differentiating $(P^0)^2=m^2c^2+|\mathbf p|^2$ gives $P^0dP^0=P^i dp_i$, so the (dy)-term vanishes. The matrix $\partial P^i/\partial p_j=\delta^{ij}$ is symmetric, so $dP^i\wedge dp_i=0$. The restricted form is therefore the pullback of $da^i\wedge dp_i$, which is nondegenerate on $B_m$.

The spaces $\mathbb R^3$ and $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ are Hausdorff second-countable manifolds; their product with $\mathbb R^3_a$ has the same properties. Product projection is a smooth submersion with global section $y=0$, establishing the asserted global quotient directly.
Along every orbit $x^0(\alpha)=x^0(0)+\alpha P^0$, with $P^0>0$, so each level $x^0=ct$ is attained at the unique parameter $\alpha=(ct-x^0(0))/P^0$.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

For a smooth Lagrangian $L:TQ\to\mathbb R$, its **fibre derivative** or
**Legendre map** is the fibre-preserving smooth map

$$\mathbb FL:TQ\to T^*Q,\qquad (\mathbb FL(q,v))(w)=\left.\frac d{ds}\right|_{s=0}L(q,v+sw).$$

In bundle coordinates it is
$\mathbb FL(q^i,v^i)=(q^i,p_i)$ with
$p_i=\partial L/\partial v^i$. This coordinate formula also shows smoothness
and that the base point $q$ is unchanged.

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Let $\mathcal D$ be an open subset of the time-dependent tangent bundle $\mathbb R\times TQ$ of a finite-dimensional smooth manifold $Q$, and let $L:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. For fixed $t$, the **fibre derivative** is the map

$$\mathbb F L(t,q,v)=(t,q,p),\qquad p(w)=\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}L(t,q,v+sw),$$

as in [[def-fibre-derivative-and-legendre-transform-of-a-lagrangian]]. In induced coordinates $p_i=\partial L/\partial v^i$.

The Lagrangian is **regular** at $(t,q,v)$ when the velocity Hessian $(\partial^2L/\partial v^i\partial v^j)$ is invertible there; regularity gives only a local inverse branch. It is **hyperregular on a declared domain** when $\mathbb F L$ is a diffeomorphism from that entire domain onto an open subset of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$.

It is **almost regular on a declared domain $\mathcal D_0\subseteq\mathcal D$** when the following are all assumed: $\mathbb F L|_{\mathcal D_0}$ has constant rank; its image $N$ is an embedded submanifold of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$; its corestriction $\mathcal D_0\to N$ is a surjective submersion (its differential is surjective at every point); and every fibre of that corestriction is connected. These hypotheses are not consequences of singularity alone.

derivations.claim: Differentiate $L(q,av)=aL(q,v)$ with respect to $a$ at $a=1$. The chain rule gives $v^iL_{v^i}=L$.

Differentiate the identity in step 1.1 with respect to $v^j$. The product rule gives $L_{v^j}+v^iL_{v^iv^j}=L_{v^j}$, hence $L_{v^iv^j}v^i=0$. For nonzero $v$ this is a nonzero kernel vector, so the Hessian is singular and the derivative of the fibre map in [F1] is not invertible.

The definition $E_L=v^iL_{v^i}-L$ and step 1.1 give $E_L=0$. The inverse function theorem's necessary invertibility condition fails by step 2.1, so regular Legendre inversion is unavailable; [F2] also makes clear that stronger almost-regular hypotheses do not follow from this degeneracy.
